newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian farmers save from rate cuts - Fischer.
newsitem.headline: Australian farmers save from rate cuts - Fischer.

text.p: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday farmers had saved A$300 million because of interest rate cuts under the conservative government, and would continue to save even more.
"The interest rate reductions which have occurred under the coalition government have saved farmers over A$300 million already with more to come," Fischer told parliament.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has cut official cash rates a total of 1.5 percentage points since July, 1996, in three separate cuts.
The Liberal-National government, elected 14 months ago, says the rate cuts have been an important factor in helping business and cutting business costs by making borrowing cheaper.
